description: Check a remote MCP server before installing it: level (risco, atencao, ok), measured signals (dead domain, consumer tunnel, no TLS, not answering as MCP, login required, suspicious text in tool descriptions, archived or stale repository, newly registered domain), server and domain facts (registration window, OV/EV organization, other domains on the same TLS certificate) and the last changes. Facts, not a certification. Take the id from list_listings. We visit every remote MCP server in the catalog: an `initialize` and a `tools/list`, without credentials and without calling any tool, again 7 days after a success. A failure counts only when confirmed on a second visit. `nivel` sums up the signals: `risco` (dead domain, consumer tunnel, no TLS), `atencao` (not answering, not MCP, suspicious text in tool descriptions, redirect to another domain, archived or stale repository, domain registered less than 90 days ago) or `ok`; empty means not checked yet. Signals: dns_morto, sem_https, tls_invalido, tunel, nao_responde, nao_mcp, texto_suspeito, redireciona_fora, repo_arquivado, repo_parado, dominio_recente, login, bloqueado. The level describes measured facts; it does not certify that a tool is safe. Local servers, skills and plugins answer `conferido: false` with `motivo: nao_remoto`. Cached for 5 minutes.
